name: Indian-style Overnight Oats
cuisine: Modern Indian fusion (a home-kitchen and café trend; flavoured like kesar-elaichi kheer or kulfi)

ingredients.name: Milk (toned, about 3% fat)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ cup (1 tbsp of it used warm for the saffron)

ingredients.name: Green cardamom (elaichi)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 pods, seeds crushed (or a scant ¼ tsp cardamom powder)

equipment: Glass jar with a lid, about 300–350 ml (a washed jam or mason jar)
Measuring cup (½ cup / ¼ cup) and measuring spoons
Small katori (bowl) for soaking the saffron
Mortar and pestle for crushing cardamom
Chopping board and small knife for the nuts
Spoon for stirring (a long spoon reaches the bottom of a jar more easily)
Microwave or small pan to warm 1 tbsp milk
Refrigerator (essential; the soak must happen in the fridge, not on the counter, because the milk and curd would sour overnight in Mumbai heat)

steps.title: Warm a little milk
steps.text: Take 1 tbsp (15 ml) of the 120 ml milk in a small katori and warm it.
steps.visualCue: Warm to the touch, steaming slightly, not boiling
steps.videoShot: A spoon of milk poured into the katori.

steps.title: Soak the saffron
steps.text: Crumble 8–10 saffron strands into the warm milk and leave it.
steps.tip: Saffron releases colour and aroma much better in warm liquid than in cold milk.
steps.visualCue: The milk turns pale yellow-orange around the threads.
steps.cameraCheck: The saffron milk in the katori
steps.videoShot: Red threads bleeding colour into the milk.

steps.title: Open the cardamom
steps.text: Press 2 green cardamom pods with your thumb until they split, and tip out the seeds. Throw away the husks.
steps.visualCue: A small heap of sticky black seeds
steps.videoShot: A thumb cracking a green pod open.

steps.title: Crush the cardamom
steps.text: Crush the seeds in a mortar and pestle until powdery.
steps.visualCue: A fine, dark-grey powder; a strong sweet, floral smell
steps.cameraCheck: The crushed cardamom in the mortar

steps.title: Chop the nuts
steps.text: Roughly chop 6 almonds (8 g) and 5–6 pistachios (4 g). Keep them in two small heaps.
steps.visualCue: Small, uneven pieces, about the size of a grain of rice
steps.cameraCheck: The two heaps of chopped nuts on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife rocking through the almonds.

steps.title: Add the oats
steps.text: Put 40 g (½ cup) rolled oats into the jar.
steps.tip: Use rolled oats, not instant or "quick" oats; instant oats turn to paste overnight.
steps.visualCue: The jar is about one-third full of flakes.
steps.cameraCheck: ½ cup oats in the jar
steps.videoShot: Oats poured from the cup into the jar.

steps.title: Add the dry flavourings
steps.text: Add 1 tsp (5 g) chia seeds, the crushed cardamom and a tiny pinch of salt.
steps.visualCue: Black chia seeds and grey cardamom specks on top of the oats
steps.videoShot: A spoon tipping chia seeds in.

steps.title: Stir the dry mix
steps.text: Stir so the chia and cardamom spread through the oats.
steps.tip: Mixing chia in while dry stops it forming a jelly lump at the bottom.
steps.visualCue: No clumps of chia; specks evenly spread

steps.title: Add the curd
steps.visualCue: A white dollop on top of the oats
steps.cameraCheck: ¼ cup curd in the jar
steps.videoShot: Curd sliding off the spoon into the jar.

steps.title: Add the milk
steps.text: Pour in the remaining 105 ml milk, then the saffron milk with its threads.
steps.visualCue: The oats are just covered with liquid; yellow streaks from the saffron
steps.videoShot: Saffron milk poured in, swirling yellow.

steps.title: Add the honey
steps.visualCue: A golden ribbon of honey on top
steps.cameraCheck: The spoon of honey over the jar

steps.title: Mix well
steps.text: Stir thoroughly, scraping the bottom and the sides of the jar, until the curd and honey are fully blended in.
steps.tip: It should look too runny now. The oats and chia soak up most of the liquid overnight.
steps.visualCue: An even, pale-cream mixture with no white curd lumps; loose and pourable, with a thin layer of milk on top
steps.videoShot: The spoon lifting a loose, milky scoop.

steps.title: Stir in the raisins and half the nuts
steps.text: Add 1 tbsp (8 g) raisins and the chopped almonds. Keep the pistachios for the morning.
steps.tip: Raisins soaked overnight plump up and add natural sweetness, so you need less honey.
steps.visualCue: Raisins and almond bits spread through the jar

steps.title: Close and refrigerate
steps.text: Put the lid on tightly and place the jar in the fridge.
steps.visualCue: Jar sealed and in the fridge
steps.cameraCheck: The closed jar on the fridge shelf
steps.videoShot: The fridge door closing on the jar.

steps.title: Check the texture in the morning
steps.visualCue: Thick and creamy, like a set kheer; the oats are soft with a slight chew; the chia is swollen and jelly-like
steps.cameraCheck: A spoonful held up to the camera
steps.videoShot: The spoon pulling up a thick scoop.

steps.title: Adjust if needed
steps.text: If it is too thick, stir in 1–2 tbsp cold milk (not counted in nutrition).
steps.visualCue: It falls slowly off the spoon instead of standing in a stiff lump.
steps.cameraCheck: The loosened oats on the spoon
steps.videoShot: A splash of milk stirred in.

steps.title: Top and serve
steps.text: Sprinkle the chopped pistachios (and a few saffron strands, if you like) on top.
steps.visualCue: Green pistachio bits on a cream-yellow surface

researchRating.basis: overnight oats are widely loved as an easy, make-ahead, no-cook breakfast, and Indian flavours (kesar badam, kulfi, thandai, curd-rice style) are popular on Indian food blogs. Points are lost because recipe vote counts for the Indian versions are small (e.g. Whisk Affair's kesar badam version shows 5/5 from 1 vote), and common complaints are a "raw" or slimy texture for people new to cold oats, and mushiness when instant oats are used.

storage: Keep it refrigerated (below 5 °C) with the lid closed. Best within 24 hours; safe for up to 2 days (Kitchen at Hoskins also says up to 2 days). Add the nuts in the morning if making it 2 days ahead, so they stay crunchy. Never leave it out of the fridge for more than about 2 hours (milk and curd sour quickly in Mumbai's heat). Freezing is not recommended: the curd separates and the oats turn watery when thawed.
leftoverRemix: Kesar oats lassi. Blend the leftover half-jar (about 130 g) with ½ cup chilled curd, 2–3 ice cubes and a pinch of cardamom until smooth. Pour into a glass and top with a few saffron strands. It turns into a thick, kesar-badam lassi-style smoothie with a different texture.
burnOff: about 5.8 km of running (405 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 8.1 km of brisk walking (about 1 hour 40 minutes at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).
